examples.title: Hello World
examples.description: A heading and a paragraph: the smallest Gramlot page.
examples.explanation: The Page class defines main(root). Each builder call adds a typed Source node; the integration hosts the page and Gramlot renders it.

examples.title: Text and links
examples.description: Headings, inline text, quotations, code and links.
examples.explanation: Follow the nested builder calls to see how text and child elements coexist. The example includes an internal anchor and literal text that is escaped rather than interpreted as markup.

examples.title: Lists
examples.description: Ordered, unordered and nested lists, plus a glossary.
examples.explanation: Local sequences supply the content. Loops create the repeated list items, while nesting expresses the document hierarchy.

examples.title: Semantic page
examples.description: A page composed from meaningful HTML landmarks.
examples.explanation: Header, navigation, article, aside and footer give the content structure. Ordinary page methods divide construction into readable sections.

examples.title: Tables
examples.description: A catalogue with headings, rows and totals.
examples.explanation: A row helper and a loop build the table from fixed data. Caption and scoped headings describe its structure; the footer presents the calculated total.

examples.title: Forms
examples.description: Native fields, choices, buttons and a slider.
examples.explanation: Try typing, selecting options and moving the slider. Reset restores defaults. The submit button is disabled: this example has no save endpoint or application event handlers.

examples.title: Native disclosure
examples.description: Expandable questions and native progress indicators.
examples.explanation: The browser supplies details/summary interaction. Progress and meter values are static; the example introduces no bindings or controllers.

examples.title: SVG shapes
examples.description: The basic SVG vocabulary inside an HTML page.
examples.explanation: The SVG builder creates shapes within a viewBox. Coordinates determine geometry, while the shared theme supplies colors through semantic CSS variables.

examples.title: SVG composition
examples.description: A scene assembled with groups, paths and repeated objects.
examples.explanation: Helper methods build houses, trees and flowers. Loops place repeated elements, and group transformations position their local coordinates.

examples.title: Cards with icons
examples.description: HTML cards with SVG icons and live Source removal.
examples.explanation: Helpers and loops build the cards. Each × button removes its labelled Source node through the browser Builder; Gramlot updates the DOM without reloading. Reload restores the initial cards. No Data binding or server synchronization is involved.

examples.title: Static report
examples.description: A summary, chart, legend and table from the same data.
examples.explanation: Separate methods build each section. SVG bar lengths and table cells use one local dataset, making the connection between values and geometry explicit.

examples.title: Complete page
examples.description: An event page with a programme, speakers, map and FAQ.
examples.explanation: The main method assembles named sections. Helpers and nested loops compose the schedule, speaker cards and SVG map from fixed local data.

examples.title: Live Source playground
examples.description: Create, update and remove Source nodes, with a small SVG animation.
examples.explanation: Builder calls create list items. Source mutations update text, color and structure. A setInterval animates an SVG attribute; removing its section disposes the timer. Works in every gallery command and in the static gallery opened from disk.

examples.title: Pointers
examples.description: Read Data with ^, =, relative, symbolic and ?attr pointers.
examples.explanation: Each ^ pointer subscribes its attribute or text to a Data path; = reads once. A datapath makes .paths relative, #node_id reaches the context of a named node, and ?attr reads an attribute of a Data node.

examples.title: Variable datapath
examples.description: One card follows the record chosen in a select.
examples.explanation: The card's datapath is itself a pointer. Choosing another record changes the context of every relative pointer below it; the DOM follows without rebuilding the page.

examples.title: Setters and defaults
examples.description: dataSetter values and control defaults, all in place at the first render.
examples.explanation: dataSetter nodes sit after the controls and in a later branch, yet the first DOM already shows their values. Controls fill an empty path with default or default_value; attr_ writes an attribute on the Data node.

examples.title: Native editing
examples.description: Text, number, range, select, date and color fields bound both ways.
examples.explanation: Each control's value is a ^ pointer. Editing writes the Data at change, or at every input when live is true; here live itself follows a checkbox.

examples.title: Checkbox and radio
examples.description: Booleans in the Data, one per checkbox and radio button.
examples.explanation: A checkbox writes true or false. Radio buttons of one group each own a boolean: choosing one writes true there and false in the others.

examples.title: Style and visibility
examples.description: visible, class, style and reactive style shortcuts.
examples.explanation: Attributes such as color, background_color, font_size and rounded compose one style attribute and follow the Data. visible hides an element and keeps its space; hidden removes it from the layout.

examples.title: Bound SVG
examples.description: SVG geometry and paint follow range and color fields.
examples.explanation: SVG presentation attributes take ^ pointers like HTML attributes. The circle's radius, the bar's width and both fills are Data values edited by native controls.

examples.title: Freeze
examples.description: Freeze structural rendering while Data keeps updating; increment a counter, remove Source items, then thaw.
examples.explanation: A frozen branch keeps reacting to Data but defers structural DOM work. Removing a child under freeze takes effect at the thaw, which builds the current Source once.

examples.title: Forms with binding
examples.description: The native form of example 06, bound to a record.
examples.explanation: The same fieldsets as HTML / SVG example 06, with every value bound to one Data record. The summary beside the form shows the record while you type.

examples.title: SVG shapes with binding
examples.description: The six shapes of example 08, resized and recolored by controls.
examples.explanation: The shapes of HTML / SVG example 08 read their size and color from the Data; sliders and a color field change them.

examples.title: Complete page with binding
examples.description: The event page of example 12, with a bound heading, filter and map.
examples.explanation: The event page of HTML / SVG example 12 reads its heading from settings, filters the schedule by speaker through visible, and highlights the chosen map stop.

examples.title: Formula
examples.description: dataFormula computes a result path from its parameters.
examples.explanation: The formula runs when a ^ parameter changes and writes its result; a = parameter is read without triggering. _if and _else choose between two results.

examples.title: Controller
examples.description: dataController reacts to Data, to a fired path and to time.
examples.explanation: A controller runs code for its effects: here it validates a value, counts fired requests, debounces with _delay and ticks a clock with _timing.

examples.title: Named logic
examples.description: Formula and controller bodies in class Logic of 03_named_logic.js.
examples.explanation: The page module exports class Logic beside Page. func names one of its methods; the method receives the resolved parameters, and a controller also its node. Named logic runs under a strict CSP.

examples.title: Inline expressions
examples.description: == expressions in text and attributes, and inline scripts.
examples.explanation: An attribute starting with == is an expression over the other attributes of its node. It follows the pointers it reads, like a formula without a result path.

examples.title: Node methods
examples.description: SET, GET, PUT, FIRE and FIRE_AFTER from button actions.
examples.explanation: Each button action calls a method of its Source node. SET notifies observers, PUT writes silently, FIRE fires also with an equal value, FIRE_AFTER fires after a delay.

examples.title: Button controller
examples.description: A button with a nested controller, click counter, modifiers and fire.
examples.explanation: A dataController nested in a button runs once per click, with button_counter and the modifier keys. fire and fire_<name> write a Data path instead of running code.

examples.title: Events
examples.description: connect_on<event> attributes for click, input, key and pointer events.
examples.explanation: connect_onclick, connect_oninput, connect_onkeydown and connect_onmouseover add one listener each. The handler runs with this set to the declaring node.

examples.title: End-to-end story
examples.description: First the local 0.2.0 story; return after the endpoint lessons for a separate 0.2.14 quote, error and recovery step.
examples.explanation: First compare setters, live editing, radio flags, formulas, SVG and freeze. After c09/c11, revisit the same inputs with a click-only dataRpc: the server quote is a snapshot, errors retain it and a successful retry clears the error.

examples.title: Lifecycle
examples.description: Core 0.2.0: observe hook order, freeze, removal and Source/DOM lookup.

examples.title: Attribute projection
examples.description: Core 0.2.0 templates/masks, then the 0.2.3 sandboxed Data preview.

examples.title: Data exchange
examples.description: Core 0.2.5: save/restore typed Data and export JSON/XML; current utility path from 0.2.10.

examples.title: Endpoint
examples.description: dataRpc calls an endpoint of the page and writes the value at its result path.
examples.explanation: The page declares with_vat with @endpoint in Python and Page.registerEndpoint in JavaScript. The author attributes of the dataRpc are the arguments; _init=True makes the call when the page starts.

examples.title: Call on change
examples.description: dataRpc follows a ^ argument, with _delay, _onCalling and _onResult.
examples.explanation: Each change of the quantity calls the endpoint 500 ms after the last edit. _onCalling and _onResult are inline code that write the status; the latest call wins.

examples.title: Call on click
examples.description: A dataRpc nested in a button, with _onError for a failing and a protected endpoint.
examples.explanation: Each click calls the endpoint. An exception answers application_error; an endpoint with auth answers not_authenticated on a server that knows no identity. _onError receives the error.

examples.title: Remote
examples.description: remote makes the content of an element a fragment built by the server.
examples.explanation: The section declares remote('details', record_id='^.record_id'). The page builds the fragment with @source in Python and Page.registerSource in JavaScript; each change of the record requests it again.

examples.title: Cached remote
examples.description: Revisit remote with a last-result cache; distinguish mounted fragments from observed calls.
examples.explanation: The rules fragment depends on the category of the product. _cachedRemote makes no request when the category is the same; _onRemote is inline code that counts the mounted fragments and writes the status.

examples.title: Data remote
examples.description: Revisit endpoint values with lazy Data; compare a bound read, an explicit snapshot and cache expiry.
examples.explanation: The menu path holds a resolver of the endpoint load_menu with cacheTime 5. The ^.menu paragraph reads it: the answer arrives with the Data event. A change of the table loads the menu again.

examples.title: Publish and subscribe
examples.description: Core 0.2.18: revisit button actions with page topics, self receivers, references and native ask.

examples.title: Parent and child messages
examples.description: Core 0.2.18: local-first publish and direct parent/child postMessage exchange.

examples.title: Actions, confirmations and references
examples.description: Core 0.2.18: action, conditional ask and explicit Source/DOM references.

examples.title: Plain and delayed buttons
examples.description: Core 0.2.19: native html_button and grouped clicks with _delay.

examples.title: Pointer templates and expressions
examples.description: Core 0.2.20: revisit CSS lengths, boolean state and formatted text with attribute pointer transforms.

examples.title: Textbox and labelbox
examples.description: Two textboxes share a customer name. Type in either one, switch live editing off and on, and move the label without rebuilding the field.

examples.title: Checkbox and labelbox
examples.description: Two checkboxes share one boolean preference. Click either caption, then disable both using the State checkbox.

examples.title: RadioButtonText and labelbox
examples.description: Choose one delivery option in each group. Change the column count and label position, and try the arrow keys inside a group.

examples.title: Multiline text and labelbox
examples.description: Two multiline fields share one note. Switch live editing and move the label while keeping the text and selection.

examples.title: Password and labelbox
examples.description: Two password fields share a sample value. The browser masks the characters; changing either field updates the other.

examples.title: Single radio buttons
examples.description: Each radio binds its own boolean. A shared group makes the choices exclusive; a separate group stays independent.

examples.title: Color and labelbox
examples.description: Choose a color in either picker. Both controls and the swatch follow the same Data value.

examples.title: Horizontal slider
examples.description: Two horizontal sliders share a numeric level. Drag or use the arrow keys; switch live editing to compare immediate and committed updates.

examples.title: Vertical slider
examples.description: Vertical and horizontal sliders share the same level. The vertical minimum is at the bottom and the maximum at the top.

examples.title: Number editing
examples.description: Try a comma decimal, an integer and an exact Decimal. Invalid text stays in the field without changing Data.

examples.title: Date editing
examples.description: Enter a calendar date or a word such as oggi or domani. Two fields share one civil date.

examples.title: Time editing
examples.description: Edit a civil time with hours, minutes and optional seconds. The two fields keep the same typed value.

examples.title: Filtering select
examples.description: Search a caption, store its code. Two fields share the same choice and the same list.

examples.title: Callback select
examples.description: Search 100 random samples generated once in this page. The callback reads a Data Bag, without a server request.

examples.title: Combo box
examples.description: Choose a suggested city or enter a different one. Two fields share the same text; suggestions do not restrict what you can write.

examples.title: Checkbox group
examples.description: Choose several notification channels. Two groups share the same comma-separated codes; clearing all choices writes null.

examples.title: Date calendar
examples.description: Pick a day or type a date. The inline calendar, popup and text-only field share the same Data value.

examples.title: Required values and length
examples.description: Invalid drafts remain visible with a message while Data keeps the last accepted value.

examples.title: Formlet and shared labels
examples.description: Arrange fields in columns and share label settings. Changing the layout preserves each field and its draft.

examples.title: GroupBox and typed copy
examples.description: Group customer data under a heading. Copy TYTX with its types or choose plain JSON from the copy menu.

examples.title: Checkbox as a switch
examples.description: A switch and a checkbox share one boolean. Compare their appearance, captions and read-only state.

examples.title: Button commands
examples.description: Compare the Gramlot command button with plain HTML. Try confirmation and a delayed command.

examples.title: Toggle button with LED
examples.description: A command button and a checkbox share a boolean. The LED and aria-pressed follow Data.

examples.title: Dropdown commands and persistence
examples.description: The main surface executes; the arrow opens the menu. Shift-select a command to run it and make it the default.

examples.title: Validation rules and callbacks
examples.description: Transformations, conditions, warnings, local callbacks and remote validation.

examples.title: Border regions and splitters
examples.description: A customer workspace divided into a header, filters, an editor and a live summary. The center uses the space left by the other regions.

examples.title: Nested borders and layout designs
examples.description: An outer workspace contains another independent borderContainer. This separates application navigation from the editor and its output.

examples.title: Rounded borders and popups
examples.description: Two nested containers share a reactive corner radius, while date and choice popups open inside the editor.

examples.title: Drawers: handles, content and retained Data
examples.description: Four drawers surround one customer workspace. Each contains useful controls or shared output, so closing a pane has a visible purpose.

examples.title: Nested regions playground
examples.description: A small application workspace built from five nested containers. Size controls let you inspect several levels of layout while real widgets keep working.

examples.title: Border events and controllers
examples.description: The example makes container notifications visible as counters and payloads, using ordinary dataController subscriptions.

examples.title: Tabs, selection and closing
examples.description: Compare fourteen working tab presentations: styles on four sides, horizontal and vertical alignment, then selection, icons, badges and closing.

examples.title: Demo carousel and live preview
examples.description: The left drawer browses every other demo as a miniature; the center lets you try the chosen demo at its normal size.
